newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ease on firm dollar after tankan.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ease on firm dollar after tankan.

text.p: * Most regionals a shade softer against dollar after the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s quarterly tankan report.
* Dollar/ringgit seen higher to 2.5270 along with firmer dollar/majors. Selling noted at 2.5250 and buying at 2.5220.
* Dollar/baht mirrors dollar/yen, with upside seen on firmer dollar/majors.
* Rupiah firmer against dollar on worry over possible liquidity tightening at month-end.
* Singapore dollar stable despite Prime Minister's call to review the strength in Singapore dollar.
Most regional currencies, except the rupiah, eased against the dollar after it surged against the yen following an uninspiring Bank of Japan (BOJ) tankan on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said the tankan reinforced belief that the BOJ was unlikely to hike interest rates in the near term.
Dollar/ringgit saw good commercial buying but the focus was on the stronger dollar/yen, which could check dollar/ringgit.
"People are selling dollar/ringgit around 2.5245/50 and buying at around 2.5220/25. That is the trading range ringgit is stuck in," said a Singapore-based U.S. bank dealer.
Dealers in Singapore said the dollar/ringgit could test 2.5300 on Wednesday and pegged good support at 2.5180.
The baht fell to 25.480-25.483 to the dollar in line with movement of major currencies, against 25.460-25.465 late on Tuesday, dealers said.
"Baht/dollar moved in a narrow range in sluggish trade just a touch above the central bank midrate," a dealer said.
Dealers said most Thai and foreign banks remained on the offer side on the open because of their long baht positions.
"The overnight rate decline on Tuesday afternoon surprised the market and it may fall further this afternoon," a dealer in Bangkok said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the dollar/baht mid-rate at 25.48 against 25.46 on Tuesday. The one-month dollar/baht swap premium was quoted at 9.00 satangs against 9.00/10.00 late on Tuesday.
The rupiah firmed against the dollar on worry over possible liquidity tightening at month-end, dealers said.
One U.S. bank dealer said Singapore operators were seen to be relatively bullish on dollars, pushing spot dollars up to a high of 2,345.25 at the opening.
"But some rises in short-dated swaps sparked worry over possible liquidity tightening which triggered renewed selling pressure on the dollar," the dealer said.

At 0400 GMT, spot rupiah was at 2,345.0/6.00 against an opening of 2,344.0/45.0. Today rupiah was at 2,343.75/44.00. There was no trading in value tomorrow due to a public holiday in the United States.

The U.S. bank dealer said there were some operators who were still upbeat on dollars because of the central bank fixing policy which has been to depreciate the rupiah by three to four points a week since the end of September.
"Some think this policy, coupled with flush supply, favours long dollar holding. But meanwhile the focus will be on the month-end first," the dealer said.

Dealer said strong local confidence that no widening of the dollar-rupiah trading band was likely in the medium-term, helped the dollar recover, following a sell-off after Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad's comments that the widening of the band was positive for foreign debt payments.
Singapore dollar maintained a neutral posture against the dollar following the Prime Minister's call to review the strength of the Singapore dollar.
Dealers expect dollar/Sing to trade above 1.3990-1.4000 level and pegged resistance at 1.4045.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Angela Tan in Singapore (65-8703083)
